field.label: Enable
field.help: Look for events at the interval below and send them to the enabled channels. Gateway alarms, CARP transitions and startup are reported straight away, and a Monit test can trigger a check itself.

field.label: Check interval
field.help: How often to look for events. Gateway alarms, CARP changes and startup arrive straight away whatever this is set to, as do Monit alerts when a test runs the check itself (see Monit services on a channel); everything else waits for the next check, so a longer interval delays it by that much. System Status is checked at most every 5 minutes and certificates hourly, either way.

field.label: Only when CARP master
field.help: Stay quiet while this firewall is the standby of a CARP pair, so only the master reports. Ignored when no CARP virtual IPs exist.

field.label: Title prefix
field.help: What to put in front of every notification title, to tell firewalls apart. Choose None when the channel already names this firewall, as a Discord webhook's bot name does.

field.label: Prefix text
field.help: Text to put in front of every notification title.

field.label: Combine messages from
field.help: Send one summary instead of separate notifications when this many events arrive in the same check. Enter 0 to always send them separately.

field.label: Gateway latency and loss
field.help: Also notify when a gateway reports high latency or packet loss, not only when it goes down.

field.label: Gateway hold time
field.help: How long a gateway must stay in its new state before it is reported, so a flapping link does not fill a channel. With no hold it is reported by the next check, which a gateway alarm triggers immediately.

field.label: Report successful logins
field.help: Report every successful login as well as failures and lockouts. Failures and lockouts are always reported when a channel takes login events.

field.label: Intrusion alert severity
field.help: Which intrusion detection alerts to report. Suricata writes many alerts, so high only is a sensible start; the Combine setting groups bursts into one message.

field.label: Daily update check
field.help: Check for firmware updates daily at around 04:00. Without it, updates are only reported once something else checks: the dashboard, the firmware page, another cron job, or configctl firmware check from a shell. Running an update, or opnsense-update -c, reports nothing.

field.label: Certificate warning (days)
field.help: Notify when a certificate or authority in System: Trust expires within this many days, and again once it has expired. Certificates are checked hourly.

field.label: System Status level
field.help: Lowest severity of System Status entries to send. Each new occurrence is reported, and so is an entry being resolved or dismissed. These are the alerts behind the bell icon in the menu bar, such as crash reports, low disk space and expired certificates. Notice also includes configuration override warnings.

field.label: State table warning (%)
field.help: Warn when the firewall state table reaches this share of its limit, and again when it drops back. Applies to channels that take the State table event.

field.label: Summary hour
field.help: Hour of the day (0 to 23) at which summaries are sent, by the first check after it starts.

field.label: Weekly summary day
field.help: Day on which weekly summaries are sent.

field.label: Monthly summary day
field.help: Day of the month (1 to 31) on which monthly summaries are sent. In a shorter month the summary goes on its last day, so 31 means the end of every month.
